Alkaloids are important in pharmacy and medicine because alkaloid-containing plants have a long history of medical use. After the first alkaloids were isolated in the 19th century, they were rapidly applied in clinical practice, and many alkaloids are still used medicinally, usually as salts [S3]. Their therapeutic importance includes central-nervous-system stimulation (cocaine, caffeine, and cathinone), hallucinogenic effects (mescaline and several indole alkaloids), and strong narcotic pain relief (morphine and codeine) [S2].
